sample_unit: de-identified cardiovascular patient notes (gender-swapped; 10,000 prompts) plus 15,000 simulated cases per model

links.outcome: Change in GPT-4o differential diagnosis accuracy when patient gender was swapped in real notes
links.effect: Significant diagnostic accuracy differences in 11 of 50 cases (22%); female patients scored lower for coronary artery disease (P<0.01), abdominal aortic aneurysm (P<1.0×10^-9), atrial fibrillation (P<0.01).
links.quote: Diagnostic accuracy across genders was determined by comparing model outputs to actual discharge diagnoses via FDR-corrected Mann-Whitney U tests, revealing significant diagnostic accuracy differences in 11 cases (22%).

links.outcome: Gender representation in LLM-generated simulated cardiovascular cases versus US prevalence
links.effect: Significant deviation from prevalence (P<0.0001); in 14 of 15 GPT-4-generated conditions (93%), males were overrepresented by a mean of 30% (SD 8.6%).
links.quote: In 14 GPT-4-generated conditions (93%), male patients were overrepresented compared to females by a mean of 30% (SD 8.6%).

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of gender bias and diagnostic accuracy disparities in GPT-4 and GPT-4o using simulated case generation and gender-swapped clinical notes from MIMIC-IV.
